title: Activation distribution normalizer and INT8 deploy harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a robust pipeline and lightweight runtime support for activation-aware INT8 (SmoothQuant-style) quantization that minimizes accuracy regressions across customer workloads while keeping latency and memory overhead acceptable. This ticket delivers three coordinated pieces: (1) a distribution normalizer pre-processing step in the calibration pipeline that stabilizes per-channel activation scales across batches and prompt lengths; (2) a calibration orchestration harness (calibration hammock) that produces deterministic per-layer/per-channel scale profiles and stores them in the model artifact catalog; (3) a runtime operator shim and kernel hook that applies the stored rescale maps with minimal kernel branching and a fallback path to FP16/alternative quant profiles if regression gates trip.

Background and motivation:
SmoothQuant-style rescaling has shown >2x INT8 accuracy improvements on activation-skewed transformers but is sensitive to calibration distribution shifts (prompt length, tokenization variance). Several customer regressions in internal pilots stemmed from a mismatch between calibration batches and live traffic activation statistics. A distribution normalizer reduces that mismatch by computing stable normalization factors across calibration shards and by providing a per-workload variance signal used by the runtime to decide on dynamic rescale application.

Goals and success criteria (high level):
- Reduce median accuracy regression (measured by token-level cross-entropy on golden prompts) to <0.5% relative to FP16 for target models when using INT8+normalizer profiles.
- Runtime latency overhead <= +3% for 4096-token context, memory overhead <= +5% on GPUs with KV cache.
- Calibration pipeline reproducibility: identical profile across repeated runs on same calibration seed 99% of layers.
- Safe rollout tooling: automatic rollback and per-model canary to avoid customer impact.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not attempt full FP8 support; FP8 profiling will be tracked in follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline produces per-layer/per-channel scale artifacts stored in the catalog with a v2 schema and provenance metadata.
Nightly quant-validation job runs on golden prompt set and fails the merge if accuracy delta > 1% on any model in the baseline set.
Runtime operator applies stored rescale maps with single-copy fusion microkernel and adds <3% latency overhead on p4d-16x when measured with bench harness.
Canary rollout flow: 5% -> 25% -> 100% gated on automated eval and SLOs, with an automatic fallback switch that can revert to FP16 instantly.
Unit and integration tests for cal-hammock, normalizer, kernel shim added and passing in CI (coverage: calibration and runtime paths).
implementation_steps: Design: finalize distribution normalizer algorithm (batch aggregation, percentile clipping, per-channel variance cap).
Cal harness: implement 'cal-hammock' service that accepts workload tokens, runs calibration shards, and outputs canonical profiles with provenance metadata.
Storage: extend model artifact schema to store per-channel rescale maps under catalog key `quant_profiles/v2`.
Runtime: implement operator shim that reads quant_profiles/v2, applies fused channel-wise rescale before matmul; add kernel selector flag 'apply_rescale_map'.
Fallback: add dynamic check in request router: if golden-prompt regression > threshold or memory overhead triggers, route to FP16 or alternative quant profile.
CI: add nightly quant-validation job that runs calibrated INT8 variants and posts metrics to the quant dashboard; block merges on regressions above threshold.
Benchmarks: run latency/cost/accuracy sweep across 6 representative models and document results in confluence and release notes.
